learningObjectives: Create concise list comprehensions for common data transformations.
Use lambda, map, filter, and reduce for functional-style operations.
Choose between traditional loops and functional expressions appropriately.

activities.title: Comprehension Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the parts of a Python list comprehension.

content.concept: A list comprehension combines an expression, an iterable, and optionally a condition to create a new list concisely.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

items: [number * 2 for number in numbers if number % 2 == 0]
descriptions: Complete list comprehension that creates a new list.
Expression applied to each selected element.
Iterates through each value in numbers.
Optional filtering condition that keeps only even numbers.

activities.title: Comprehension Builder
activities.instruction: Build a comprehension that squares only even numbers.

content.concept: List comprehensions can transform values and filter elements in one readable expression.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

options: [number ** 2 for number in numbers if number % 2 == 0]

activities.title: Functional Tool Explorer
activities.instruction: Choose the functional tool that matches the operation.

content.concept: lambda creates small anonymous functions, map transforms elements, filter selects elements, and reduce combines values into a single result.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Creates a small anonymous function expression.
Applies a function to each item of an iterable.
Keeps items for which a function returns a truthy result.
Combines iterable elements cumulatively into one value; imported from functools.

activities.title: Transformation Selector
activities.instruction: Choose the operation that produces the target result.

content.concept: Different functional operations solve different problems: transformation, filtering, or aggregation.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: reduce(lambda a, b: a + b, numbers)
